title: How do we draw a line parallel to a given line?
description: A line l and a line t meet at X with a sixty degree angle. The board marks a point Y on t, copies the angle at Y to draw m, and finds that the equal corresponding angles make m parallel to l. Keeko doubts that m should use the other angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: copy the angle at X to the same corner at Y, and equal corresponding angles make the two lines parallel. Watch for students who copy the other angle of the linear pair.

source: A line l and a transversal t meet at X, and the angle a between them is 60°. Draw a line m through a point Y on t that is parallel to l, and name the angles that are equal.
video_script.why: The child draws a parallel line by copying an angle and sees why the corresponding angles make the lines parallel.
video_script.substitution: The book's own activity: copy the angle a at X to the same corner at Y with tracing paper or a protractor, and see that the two lines appear parallel.
video_script.anchor: A line l and a line t meeting at X with the angle a of sixty degrees, and a point Y on t below X.
video_script.wrong_answer: draw m at one hundred and twenty degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks m should use the other angle of the linear pair.
video_script.payoff_line: The line m is parallel to the line l.

final_answer.value: m is parallel to l, since the corresponding angles a and b are both 60°
final_answer.spoken: the line m is parallel to the line l, since the corresponding angles eigh and b are both sixty degrees

hold_back: m is parallel to l, since the corresponding angles a and b are both 60°
maths_rules: the other angle of the linear pair at X is 180 - 60 = 120, so there are two different angles, 60 and 120
mark a point Y on t
draw m through Y so that it makes a 60 degree angle with t, on the same side as a, by copying a with tracing paper or measuring with a protractor
the angle b at Y is 60 degrees and the angle a at X is 60 degrees; they are corresponding angles and they are equal
when corresponding angles are equal, the two lines are parallel
the slip: the 120 degree angle is in a different corner from a, so copying it does not give a parallel line
video_script.design: One figure stays on the stage. The point Y is marked, the line m is drawn in a second colour through Y, and the angles a and b are marked in the same colour.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A line that crosses two other lines is called a transversal.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Angles in the same corner at the two crossings are in matching positions.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Such angles are called corresponding angles.
